R0068.title: After-Sales Rights Abuse
R0068.definition: Malicious exploitation and excessive use of rights granted by the platform.
R0068.description: For example, national regulations require online shopping platforms to offer 7-day no-questions-asked returns. Buyers exploit this mechanism to use products or services for free and then initiate a return within 7 days.
R0068.influence: Causes financial losses to the platform or sellers.

references.title: Generali China Life Beijing 315 Risk Alert: Resist Black-Grey Market, Protect Information Security

observables: A single account or device issues a dense burst of return requests shortly before the 7-day no-questions-asked return window expires
Accounts with return rates far above normal users concentrate their orders in specific product categories or stores
Return requests are filed shortly after delivery with no normal usage traces, and the stated return reasons are highly templated
A single shipping address or payment account is linked to multiple high-return-rate accounts

R0068-001.title: Malicious Complaints
R0068-001.definition: Filing malicious complaints against a trading platform or against merchants on a trading platform.
R0068-001.description: Black-market actors aim to gain improper benefits or force the target to be penalized, filing malicious complaints against trading platforms through regulators, or against merchants through the trading platform. Common tactics include bulk-complaining about boilerplate clauses such as advertising-law prohibited terms or labeling defects, and demanding payment in exchange for withdrawing the complaint, forming a professional complaint-extortion chain that inflicts financial and reputational losses on both platforms and merchants.
R0068-001.influence: Causes financial or reputational losses to the platform or sellers.

references.title: Black-Grey Market Preying on Consumer Rights Advocates

observables: A single complainant files multiple complaints against different merchants through regulators or the platform within a short window, with near-identical wording
A complaint is immediately followed by conditions for withdrawal plus a payment account, exhibiting a typical extortion script
The complainant's historical complaints concentrate on boilerplate clauses such as advertising-law prohibited terms or labeling defects
The complaint account was recently registered, and its real-name information does not match its prior consumption behavior

R0068-002.title: Malicious Claims
R0068-002.definition: Bulk-purchasing expired, unlisted, or counterfeit goods and filing tenfold compensation claims.
R0068-002.description: Using bulk searches, data scraping, and similar methods to find expired, counterfeit, substandard, or non-compliant products (e.g., containing advertising law prohibited terms). After placing orders, the buyer complains about the seller's violations and demands large sums of money in exchange for withdrawing the complaint.
R0068-002.influence: Sellers are extorted into paying large sums or bear penalties; platform complaint workloads and compliance costs rise, and normal business order is disrupted.

references.title: Meituan Reports Jan-Aug Black-Grey Market Crackdown Results: Over 50 Million Yuan Involved

observables: Accounts bulk-order expired, counterfeit, or advertising-law-violating products with abnormally high order concentration
Complaints are filed immediately after ordering and demand large sums in exchange for withdrawal, displaying professional claimant scripts
A single device or shipping address is linked to multiple claim accounts, with claim amounts mostly pegged at the tenfold-compensation cap
Request patterns from bulk product-compliance searches or scraping are observable in the site's search logs
